summary: One task of a round of the IO board component research (hardware/docs/Research.md)
logs: FU: 19 agents started (11 planned, 8 of 21 free used); 79 items for follow-up

items.requirement: Sized for about 49.7 A: the board's draw from the pack at the 6.0 V floor with the four TPS55285 at 6.35 A, nominal at an assumed 90 %. Round 1 sized both for 12.23 A (V90). No pack disconnect passed round 1: its one shortlisted candidate, R5460N212AF-TR-FE, failed the open balance lead (V107) in FU-B1, and FU-B3 found none
items.source: IOBoard.md, Pack path current and Pack reconnect; Supply.md, Not known
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.function: overvoltage protection; reverse-polarity protection; inrush limiting
items.requirement: The DC input's overvoltage threshold, non-destructive (owner, 2026-09-30): round 1 left the overvoltage protection without a part. FU-B3 did not requalify the LM74800QDRRRQ1 for the reverse-polarity protection and the inrush limiting
items.source: IOBoard.md, Overvoltage protection, Reverse-polarity protection, Inrush limiting, and Not known under Power
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.requirement: A signal the coprocessor reads that tells the DC input from the pack: a DC-input-present input or the DC input voltage, on an RP2354B input or an expander pin within the pin budget. Answered under Raised by P1: V271: One signal: the DC input voltage through a divider into one ADC input of the measurement coprocessor, GPIO 40 to 47. The firmware compares it with the thresholds, so it serves the source status and the DC input brownout detection (owner, 2026-10-01) V276: As V271: the DC input voltage on one ADC input of the measurement coprocessor, serving both (owner, 2026-10-01)
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.requirement: Detects the DC input falling below a threshold, which the coprocessor reads; non-destructive (owner, 2026-09-30). Its threshold and the time below it are not stated. The source selection's undervoltage gate is 10.1 V falling and 11.0 V rising (V88). Answered under Raised by P1: V272: Trips at 11.0 V falling and resets at 11.5 V rising, above the source selection's 10.1 V handover (V88) (owner, 2026-10-01) V273: 10 ms (owner, 2026-10-01) V274: As V272: 11.0 V falling, 11.5 V rising (owner, 2026-10-01) V275: As V273: 10 ms (owner, 2026-10-01)
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.requirement: Thresholds for about 49.7 A, against 3.0 V a cell (F9) and 0 to 55 °C (owner, 2026-09-30), at or below the pack's 90 A continuous. Round 1 set them for 12.23 A (V150). Answered under Raised by P1: V284: 60 A, about 20 % above the 49.7 A nominal draw and below the pack's 90 A continuous (owner, 2026-10-01)
items.source: IOBoard.md, Pack overcurrent protection and Pack temperature
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

value.quantity: pack full-charge voltage used for sizing (V, upper bound)
value.refutation_tried: checked the SLS XTRON vendor-page description at IOBoard.md:395 -- it states 7.4 V nominal and no per-cell charge limit, so 4.2 V/cell is not vendor-confirmed; already raised as V92 ('for research'), not re-raised

value.quantity: board draw from the pack at the 6.0 V floor, nominal (A)
value.refutation_tried: recomputed the four-converter subtotal from the page's own per-converter figures: 3 servo converters at 9.9 A each (IOBoard.md:359) = 29.7 A, plus the adjustable supply at 17.6 A (IOBoard.md:381) = 47.3 A, matching the stated four-converter figure exactly; adding the display's 1.4 A (IOBoard.md:395) and the second RP2354B's 0.2 A (IOBoard.md:120) gives 48.9 A, about 0.8 A short of the stated 49.7 A, with the remainder (the main RP2354B's and other unitemized logic current) not broken out anywhere in the tree; the underlying 90% pack-side efficiency is explicitly 'not stated' and remains open at V90/V105/V111 ('for research')

value.quantity: stated failure reasons of the pack disconnect candidates
value.value: each candidate failed an open balance lead (V107), the reconnect condition (V93, V94) or the per-cell floor (V95)
value.refutation_tried: read every P2, P3, rerank and P4 return for R5's pack disconnect across T3, FU-B1 and FU-B3 -- only one candidate was ever shortlisted, R5460N212AF-TR-FE, refuted in both FU-B1 (hardware/research/round1/FU-B1/032-P4-datasheet-R5.json) and FU-B3 specifically on the balance-lead-open check (V107); the same P4 return shows it passing the reconnect-condition (V93, V94) and per-cell-floor (V95) checks. No candidate's recorded failure is the reconnect condition or the per-cell floor; the claim is not supported by the primary files read for this task

value.quantity: nominal board draw from the pack at the 6.0 V floor
value.value: about 49.7 A with the display, the logic rails and the second RP2354B included; about 47.3 A from the four TPS55285 converters alone at an assumed 90 % efficiency
value.source: IOBoard.md:359 (Pack path current): 'at the 6.0 V floor the four converters at 6.35 A draw about 47.3 A at an assumed 90 %, and the board about 49.7 A ... nominal figures'.
value.refutation_tried: The page itself calls these 'nominal figures' with 'no upper bound' until the protection threshold is set (IOBoard.md:395). The 90 % efficiency from the pack is unverified (already raised as V140, Research.md:836, 'for research'); not re-raised here. Holds as the nominal, not maximum, draw this follow-up's threshold has to clear.

value.quantity: charger efficiency and resulting charge current
value.value: assumed 90 %: 13.5 W, about 1.6 A into a full pack at 8.4 V; a 2 A charger (BQ25887 reference figure) uses the whole 13.5 W above 6.75 V
value.source: IOBoard.md:400 (Charge current): 'At an assumed 90 % that is 13.5 W ...'.
value.refutation_tried: No source is given for 90 %; the same unverified figure as V139 (Research.md:835, 'for research'), already under Raised by P1 and not re-raised. The arithmetic (15 W x 0.9 = 13.5 W; 13.5 W / 8.4 V = 1.607 A) holds.

value.value: not stated: whether it is the RP2354B's own USB port or a separate USB-C connector
value.source: IOBoard.md:407 (Not known): 'Whether the charger's USB-C input is the RP2354B's USB port or a connector of its own: not stated (F8, R7, round 2)'.
value.refutation_tried: Matches V148 (Research.md:844, 'for research'), already under Raised by P1; not re-raised here.

followUps.reason: function the row names that P2 did not return: IOBoard.md, Power, Overvoltage protection row: 'a transient the protection absorbs (V85) stays within the rating of the part that absorbs it', and V85 asks what the DC input's protection absorbs; Research.md Round 2, Rules of stage 1, puts the power input's protection in stage 1 and in R5 (connector protection for stage 2 lists the signal, sensor, balance-lead, link and heartbeat connectors, not the power inputs; IOBoard.md line 575 agrees). P2's survival rows for reverse-polarity protection, overvoltage protection, inrush limiting and source selection all assume TVS2701DRBR (60 V for 10 us clamped to at most 37.3 V; V85 'found'), P2's own report 'input transient clamp gap' says the clamp 'needs a function of its own', and P2 returned no entry for it, so selection.json (hardware/research/round2/selection.json, R5) has no clamp. P2 dropped TVS2701DRBR and SMBJ26CA-13-F from the overvoltage function as 'not candidates for this function'. Data P2 already read for the missing entry: TVS2701DRBR JLCPCB C2878109 stock 155, presale 118 (P2 file jlc_summary.txt, 2026-10-02T11:55:24Z), 2 placements, need 10, gate 50; SMBJ26CA-13-F C135063 63/62 clamps at 42.1 V at 14.2 A, above 37.3 V (FU-B3 P2 report, 2026-09-29T15:33:18Z). Not ranked, no second source, lifecycle and Digi-Key not recorded.

found_values.value: Yes, up to the input limit, 3.0 A at 5 V (15 W, F8), less the charge current. The BQ25723's NVDC path regulates VSYS at the minimum system voltage when the battery is depleted or removed ('Even with a depleted battery, the system ...', 9.3; BATDRV pin: 'BATFET is in linear mode to regulate VSYS at minimum system voltage when battery is depleted'). found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/bq25723.pdf (SLUSE64, HTTP 200, 4,002,198 bytes), pin 21 BATDRV and the VSYS_MIN section

found_values.value: Yes: USB-C is the only charge source (F8), so a pack at the 3.0 V floor recovers on the bench only if it charges while the floor disconnect is open. The charger need not sit on the cells' side: with the MAX17320G22+ as the protector, 'All discharge-only faults are released when the charger is connected', and the BQ25723 holds VSYS from VBUS so the RP2354B can write ChargeCurrent (reset 0000h). Below VSYS_MIN the charge is clamped to 384 mA. The release of the discharge fault on charger connection also reconnects the pack to the board's load: R5's reconnect condition (IOBoard.md Pack reconnect) has to cover it

found_values.value: The DC input's cut-off trips above 20.0 V and at or below 22.0 V at every tolerance corner. 22.0 V is the TPS55285's highest recommended input; the servo converters share the bus. 20 V is taken to include the DC source's tolerance, because the tree states 12 to 20 V with none. With the LM7480x OV comparator, V(OVR) 1.195 V to 1.267 V, and a divider of 17.06, it trips at 20.39 V to 21.61 V, or 20.35 V to 21.66 V with 0.1 % resistors. It releases only below V(OVF) 1.091 V to 1.159 V, which is 18.61 V to 19.77 V at the input. A source between 18.6 V and 20 V that trips once, for example on a transient, stays cut off (report)

found_values.value: Yes: the reverse-polarity, overvoltage and inrush protection sit on the 2S pack input as well as on the DC input. The pack input takes the same mis-connections the owner names for V267; applying V267 to the pack input is an inference, stated as such. One LM7480x controller on each input gives all three with the ideal-diode OR of the source selection (9.5.1)
found_values.source: V267 Answer, Research.md:973 at checkout f06c3ae0d570; https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm7480-q1.pdf SNOSD95C 9.5.1

found_values.value: 2.0 A peak on each input at plug-in, at every tolerance corner. No source in the tree states a limit; 2.0 A is the display's own 2 A peak (prerequisite 7), chosen as the bound. The LM7480x sets it with a capacitor on HGATE: I_INRUSH = I(HGATE) x C_OUT / CdVdT, I(HGATE) source 39 uA to 75 uA (55 uA typical). With CdVdT -5 % and C_OUT +20 %, a design at 1.16 A nominal stays at or under 2.0 A. Converters that start during the ramp add their current; their own UVLO or enable holds them off and is not counted here
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm7480-q1.pdf SNOSD95C 7.5 I(HGATE) source current, 9.3.2.2; Research.md prerequisite 7

found_values.value: The DC input counts as absent below 10.1 V falling and present above 11.0 V rising, set with the LM7480x EN/UVLO comparator: V(UVLOR) 1.195 V to 1.267 V, V(UVLOF) 1.091 V to 1.159 V, a divider of 8.936. With 0.1 % resistors the falling threshold is 9.73 V to 10.38 V and the rising 10.66 V to 11.34 V. The requirement is the bounds: the falling threshold's lowest corner stays above the pack's highest 8.45 V, and the rising threshold's highest corner is at or below 11.4 V. 12 V is taken as the lowest the DC source delivers with its tolerance. I(EN/UVLO) is 200 nA at most, so the divider's parallel resistance stays under about 30 kOhm. The DC input brownout detection's 11.0 V falling and 11.5 V rising (V272) lie above this handover
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm7480-q1.pdf SNOSD95C 7.5 V(UVLOR), V(UVLOF), I(EN/UVLO), 9.3.4; V272 Answer, Research.md

found_values.value: 0 ms on both rails. A 3.3 V dip resets the RP2354B and the reset supervisor of F12; a 5 V dip resets the display, which stops the heartbeat. The ideal-diode OR keeps the bus up: on DC removal the pack path's MOSFET body diode conducts at once and DGATE turns on in 2.8 us typical, 3.8 us maximum; on DC connection the pack path's DGATE turns off in 0.5 us typical, 0.875 us maximum
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm7480-q1.pdf SNOSD95C 7.6 tDGATE_ON(dly), tDGATE_OFF(dly); monostable page at 23c82ca

found_values.value: Option 1, 90 % for every converter: 50.4 A at the 6.0 V floor and 52.1 A at a 5.8 V bus. Four TPS55285 at 6.35 A deliver 255.3 W (IOBoard.md, Adjustable supply budget), 283.7 W in; the 5 V rail at its 2.08 A peak (display 2.0 A, TCAN1472VDRQ1 0.08 A) 11.6 W in; the 3.3 V rail at its 1,475 mA summed maxima 5.4 W in; the encoder supply 1.3 W in; 302.0 W in all, plus the load-cell excitation's 0.06 A, linear from the bus. Option 2 has no datasheet figure: the TPS55285 states its ILIM_AVG as 7 A minimum and 8 A typical with no maximum and guarantees no efficiency. The load returning alone never reconnects the pack, and the DC input present does not, since the DC input never charges the pack (F8). The class is a charger-gated release: the R5460 F version releases 'after connecting a charger', and the BQ40Z family recovers from CUV with Protection Configuration[CUV_RECOV_CHG] = 1 only with every cell at or above CUV:Recovery and charging detected

found_values.value: Either order. The one IO board part supplied from both rails is the TCAN1472VDRQ1 (VCC from the 5 V rail, VIO from the 3.3 V rail); it has undervoltage protection on VCC (UVCC falling 3.5 V to 4.0 V) and on VIO (UVIO falling 1.4 V to 1.5 V) and passive behaviour when unpowered (TXD leakage plus or minus 1 uA at VCC = VIO = 0 V). The 5 V rail feeds the display through the TPS25947, which blocks reverse current. The parts that see 5 V signals while 3.3 V is down take them: AM26LV32E outputs Ioff plus or minus 100 uA at VCC 0 V; TCAN3413 unpowered bus leakage
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tcan1472-q1.pdf SLLSFW8A features, UVCC, UVIO, ILKG_TXD(OFF); https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/am26lv32e.pdf Ioff row; https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tcan3413.pdf SLLSFS8A

found_values.value: Yes: with the 2S pack's power leads connected and its balance lead unplugged, or one balance wire open, the disconnect holds the pack off, with the USB-C charger connected or not. F9 reads the 3.0 V floor per cell from the balance lead, and a pack-voltage floor does not bound a cell; with the lead open no cell is read, so only a held-off pack keeps F9
found_values.source: F9 Answer, Research.md:679; IOBoard.md Discharge floor row at checkout f06c3ae0d570

found_values.value: 250 mA nominal, 233 mA to 267 mA: above the encoder's steady 160 mA at 5 V and 100 mA at 12 V (V102). It is the encoder converter's own output current limit in both jumper positions, because the F4 jumper selects the converter's feedback divider; the converter runs from the input bus, so a short on the encoder cable leaves the 5 V rail and the display supply untouched. The encoder's power-on inrush runs into this limit for about 11.6 ms at the lowest corner
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55288.pdf SLVSF01B 6.5 VSNS 28 mV to 32 mV at IOUT_LIMIT 10111100b; Omron E6B2-C note *1

Values against the Pack charger rows: VBUS 3.5 to 26 V (covers 5 V, rated far above 5.5 V); input current limit up to 6.35 A / 10 A in 50 / 100 mA steps for 10 / 5 mOhm RAC (covers 500 mA, 1.5 A, 3 A); 1 to 5 cells with 2S set by the CELL_BATPRESZ divider; charge current up to 16.2 A in 128 mA steps at 5 mOhm RSR (covers 2.37 A); charge voltage register covers 8.4 V; host-terminated by CHRG_INHIBIT like the BQ25723; 5 mOhm RSR is the POR setting (RSNS_RSR = 1b, text near line 1652) and SRP-SRN is -0.5 to 0.5 V both absolute and recommended, so 0.249 V at 49.7 A, 0.300 V at 60 A, 0.334 V at 66.8 A with 5 mOhm (12.4 W in the shunt at 49.7 A, same as the BQ25723's RSR). P2 dropped the LTC4020 (read as C2858365, #PBF) by sizing RCS at 21 mOhm for the 2.37 A charge current. The data sheet (Rev. E, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ltc4020.pdf, safari client, read 2026-10-02T12:32:03Z) sets ICSMAX = 0.05 V / RCS but gives RNG/SS (pin 15, effective range 0 to 1 V) as a fraction of ICSMAX, so RCS follows the pack current, not the charge current: RCS = 4 mOhm gives ICSMAX 12.5 A, RNG/SS about 0.19 V sets 2.37 A, and CSP-CSN is 0.267 V at 66.8 A against the -0.3 to 0.3 V absolute maximum (no separate recommended range is stated). Buck-boost with 4.5 to 55 V VIN (covers 5 V, rated to 55 V), UVLO rising 3.6 to 4.4 V; float voltage by divider (8.4 V, +-0.5 %); the system load is on the converter output, the pack behind the PowerPath FET and RCS (instant-on for a flat pack); the NTC pin (1.35 V / 0.3 V limits at 50 uA) reads the pack NTC through a scaling network; ILIMIT programs the average inductor current (about the input current in boost mode, 45 to 60 mV across RSENSEA at 20 V/V) and can be driven by a resistor or a sink, so the 500 mA / 1.5 A / 3 A states are external; the accuracy of the input limit is not read. Limits: C/10 termination is 5 mV (3 to 7 mV) across RCS, 1.25 A (0.75 to 1.75 A) at 4 mOhm; the E grade is tested over 0 to 85 C junction, -40 to 125 C by design (Note 2); 12.35 W-class shunt loss at 49.7 A as for the BQ25723. ranking.reason: Unchanged: 5 mOhm RSR is a documented option (RSNS_RSR = 1b) with SRP-SRN at 0.300 V at the 60 A trip; passes every value; JLCPCB 214 and Digi-Key 4528.

Rank 2. P2's reason for dropping it does not hold: SLUSD83C 9.6.3 states "resistors of other values can also be used" for the RSR, and at 5 mOhm SRP-SRN is 0.334 V at 66.8 A, inside the 0.5 V range. The 5 mOhm use is outside the RSNS_RSR options (10 or 20 mOhm): the register code is half the current, the charge-current accuracy is tabulated at 10 mOhm only, and RSNS_RSR = 1b means 20 mOhm here and 5 mOhm on the BQ25723, so the firmware differs. The BQ25723 states 5 mOhm as an option, so it ranks first.

Rank 3. Same family and the same 5 mOhm reading as the BQ25713 (see its reason); the interface is SMBus (address 09h) and the register map differs (ChargeVoltage REG0x15, IIN_HOST REG0x3F). Digi-Key stock is 406, the thinnest of the family.
Rank 4. The BQ25713 with VAP mode, on the same data sheet, with the same 5 mOhm reading. JLCPCB stockCount 71 is 21 above the gate of 50.

Rank 5. It passes every value with RCS sized from the pack current: 4 mOhm gives 0.267 V at 66.8 A, and RNG/SS scales the charge to 2.37 A; P2's 21 mOhm sized ICSMAX at the charge current. It ranks under the BQ257xx parts: the float reference is +/-1 % over temperature (4.242 V a cell at the top, 8 mV under the 4.25 V per-cell overvoltage), a 3 A input limit needs 20 mOhm inductor sense resistors that give 2.25 to 3.0 A, the input-limit accuracy at 1.5 A and 500 mA is not stated, RCS dissipates 9.9 W at 49.7 A, VOUT rises to VOUTMAX with the pack disconnected (9.24 V at 110 % of float), and the Digi-Key lead time is 49 weeks.
Rank 6. Same 5 mOhm reading; the recommended SRP-SRN range is -0.35 to 0.35 V, so 0.334 V at 66.8 A leaves 4.6 % of margin, against 33 % on the BQ25713 (0.5 V).
Rank 7. Same as the BQ25700A: recommended SRP-SRN -0.35 to 0.35 V, 0.334 V at 66.8 A. First data sheet May 2017.

dropped_from_p3.reason: USB-only operation and charging with the floor disconnect open are not shown. The BQ25731 has no BATFET ("BATFET Power Path: No", Device Comparison Table), so VSYS is the converter output and the battery node. SLUSE66A (read 2026-10-02T12:36:55Z) states no VSYS regulation with the battery removed or held off: CELL_BATPRESZ low only resets ChargeCurrent() and disables charge (pin 18, 9.6.2), ChargeVoltage returns to 4.2 V (Table 9-2), and 9.3.21.5 says only that the converter keeps operating with charge disabled. The input limit at the 5 mOhm RAC is tabulated from 600 to 1000 mA (0x0800H) upward, so a limit at or under 500 mA is not shown either. It passes the other values: VBUS 3.5 to 26 V, 1 to 5 cells, 8.4 V +/-0.6 %, charge current to 16.256 A, SRP-SRN -0.5 to 0.5 V (0.334 V at 66.8 A at 5 mOhm), JLCPCB stockCount 1125 and canPresaleNumber 1122 (2026-10-02T12:42:10Z), Digi-Key stock 2079 (2026-10-02T12:31:24Z), TI page ACTIVE (12:42:31Z). A bench test of VSYS with the pack held off would settle it (not measured). It would remove the external BATFET.

Battery path current: SRP with respect to SRN is -0.3 to 0.3 V absolute maximum and RBAT_SNS is listed at 5 mOhm only (SLUSEN5A 5.1 and 5.3, read 2026-10-02T12:36:55Z): 0.300 V at the 60 A trip, at the limit, and 0.334 V at 66.8 A, above it. P2's reason (no system output) does not hold as stated: the data sheet's MPPT note puts the system load in parallel with the battery. The sense range fails it.

ranking.reason: Unchanged: runs from 2.85 V, so from the 3.3 V rail as well as VBUS; dead-battery Rd; I2C with interrupt; states its Rp-change time.
Unchanged: pin outputs only; VDD 4.5 V minimum ties it to VBUS or a 5 V rail; no Rp-change time stated.
Rank 3. Pins only (GPIO mode), dead-battery Rd stated, runs from the 3.3 V rail rather than VBUS; VDD has to ramp within 25 ms, a start-up figure for P5. Stock 2089 at JLCPCB.
Rank 4. The industrial-grade sibling of the TUSB320LAI with the same values; Digi-Key stock 654 is the thinnest of the family.
Rank 5. I2C with an interrupt and a stated Sink power-up mode, VDD 2.8 to 5.5 V; needs firmware to pass the limit to the charger. Same maker and class as the first-ranked FUSB303B.

Rank 6. A USB PD sink controller: pins in NVM configuration 3 give 1.5 A and 3.0 A, but the NVM has to be programmed and the part negotiates PD, which the board does not use. Runs from VBUS (VDD 4.1 to 22 V).
Rank 7. Powers up as DRP and a sink-only port needs an I2C write of MODE_SELECT after every reset; VDD 4.5 to 5.5 V ties it to VBUS or a 5 V rail. JLCPCB stock 695.
Rank 8. A TCPC: it needs a Type-C port manager in the RP2354B firmware, the heaviest of the candidates; JLCPCB stockCount 229.

report.figure: RSR other than 10 or 20 mOhm on the BQ257xx family
report.value: The BQ25713 data sheet states "The SRP and SRN pins are used to sense voltage drop across RSR with default value of 10 mOhm. However, resistors of other values can also be used", with "no more than 20 mOhm is suggested". The BQ25710, BQ25703A and BQ25700A carry the same sentence. RSNS_RSR selects 10 or 20 mOhm (1b = 20 mOhm on these parts, 5 mOhm on the BQ25723) and PSYS is limited to 10 and 20 mOhm. With a 5 mOhm RSR the charge-current register holds half the current and the charge-current accuracy is not tabulated. P2's drop reason "RSR 10 or 20 mOhm only" does not hold for the battery path current
report.source: bq25713.pdf SLUSD83C 9.3 PSYS text and 9.6.3 (read 2026-10-02T12:36:55Z); bq25710.pdf SLUSD20B, bq25703a.pdf SLUSCU1A, bq25700a.pdf SLUSCQ8A (read 2026-10-02T12:46:06Z); bq25723.pdf SLUSE64 ChargeOption1 RSNS_RSR (12:36:55Z)

report.figure: SRP-SRN at a 5 mOhm RSR against each part's range
report.value: 0.249 V at 49.7 A, 0.300 V at 60 A, 0.334 V at 66.8 A. BQ25723, BQ25713, BQ25713B, BQ25710: -0.5 to 0.5 V recommended and absolute maximum, 33 % margin at 66.8 A. BQ25703A, BQ25700A: -0.35 to 0.35 V recommended, 4.6 % margin. BQ25756: -0.3 to 0.3 V absolute maximum, 0.334 V exceeds it. LTC4020: CSP-CSN -0.3 to 0.3 V absolute maximum, no recommended range, 4 mOhm gives 0.267 V at 66.8 A. The 5 mOhm RSR dissipates 12.35 W at 49.7 A and 18 W at 60 A (computed)

report.value: selection.json of round 2 still holds round 1's FU-B3 choices for R7: BQ25713RSNR for Pack charger and Power path, MAX17320G22+ for Cell balancing, Pack overcurrent protection and Bench pack balance lead, FUSB303BTMX for Charger input limit, no part for Pack cells. report.figure: LTC4020 sense resistor and charge-current sizing
report.value: RCS = 0.05 / ICSMAX, with RNG/SS scaling the charge current as a fraction of ICSMAX: RCS = 4 mOhm gives ICSMAX 12.5 A and about 0.19 V on RNG/SS (50 uA x 3.8 kOhm) sets 2.37 A. report.value: ILMAX = 0.05 / RSENSE with VSENS 45 to 60 mV: 20 mOhm sense resistors give 2.25 to 3.0 A, so the limit can fall to 2.25 A, 25 % under 3.0 A. report.figure: LTC4020 system rail range and termination
report.value: VOUT(MIN) with a depleted pack is 85 % of float (7.14 V) and VOUTMAX with the pack disconnected is 110 % of float (9.24 V) with equal dividers, so the system rail is above the 6.0 to 8.4 V pack range while USB-C charges. parts.refutation: 'per-cell floor' fails on the datasheet's stated figures. SLUSBV4D 5.5 gives scaling factor K 0.198 to 0.202 for VC1-VSS and VC2-VC1 (+/-1 %, +/-30 mV at 3.0 V) and ADC gain error +/-0.2 % typ, +/-0.8 % max with the unit '/FSR' (VFS = VREF1, about 1.22 V), over -0.1 V to 0.8 x VFS. At the cell input (K = 0.2) 0.8 % of FSR is 48.6 to 49.2 mV; with K and the 157 uV offset (0.8 mV) the worst case is +/-79.4 to +/-80.0 mV, over the 75 mV of V95. P2's 'about +/-54 mV' reads the gain error as a percentage of the reading (24 mV + 30 mV); the datasheet does not say that. The TRM (SLUUBT5C) states no cell-voltage accuracy either; it offers Calibration:Voltage:Cell Gain (data flash 12101), which could remove K and the gain error at a calibration point, but no datasheet figure bounds the residual drift (150 ppm/degC) over 0 to 50 degC. The same rows are in the BQ40Z50-R2 and BQ4050 datasheets. Also read, not refuting: the datasheet 6.3.2 lists an 'open cell connection permanent failure' that the TRM has no section for (its section 4 list has none); balance lead open rests on the pull-down and CUV logic as P2 states.

data.ruling: The refutation does not stand. Its only failed figure is the per-cell floor measured against a +/-75 mV band, and +/-75 mV is not a requirement value. No source on the page sets that band. F9 sets the floor at 3.0 V a cell, read per cell from the balance lead. IOBoard.md (Pack disconnect, Discharge floor) gives no tolerance. The owner marked V95 "for research" (owner, 2026-09-28). V95 asks what tolerance the trip point holds over 0 to 50 degC, which is a property of the part. It does not set a limit for parts to meet. The 75 mV in the requirement text ("F9; V95 found") comes from round 1's finding on the R5460x212AF datasheet (x0.975 to x1.025 at Ta 25 degC only; FU-B1/005-P2-R5.json, FU-B3/002-P2-R5.json). That is another candidate's figure, carried over as a gate. It is not an owner answer and not a specification value. The verifier's reading of the datasheet is correct, and it corrects the figure P2 found for V95. P2's "about +/-54 mV" treats the gain error as a percentage of the reading. The datasheet's unit is /FSR (percent of full-scale range), so P2's figure stands corrected. On the datasheet maxima, the cell-channel error at 3.0 V is about +/-80 mV. That assumes FSR = VFS (about 1.22 V). If FSR spans -VFS to +VFS, the error is wider, about +/-128 mV. The datasheet states no cell-voltage accuracy and no bound limited to 0 to 50 degC. The maxima apply over -40 to 85 degC. This corrected figure is the V95 value to record: 3.0 V is the nominal trip point, and the band is about +/-80 mV. The part still meets the floor. CUV:Threshold is a data-flash value from 0 to 32767 mV in 1 mV steps. A setting of about 3080 mV (3128 mV under the wider FSR reading) makes 3.0 V the lowest trip at every tolerance corner. A production cell-gain calibration (Calibration:Voltage:Cell Gain, data flash 12101) narrows the band, but no figure bounds what is left after it. Every other datasheet and stock figure was confirmed by the verifiers and not disputed.

data.ruling: The refutation does not stand. The figure is tested by the P4 rule in tools/research/round1.js:314. Under that rule the list must name every requirement that IOBoard.md, the answers and the values found for research set for the function, and no listed value may be weaker than its source. V80's found value is a fact about the display, not a requirement on the link-supply switch. The answer is "No": the display's native USB-C VBUS is tied directly to its 5V net. Research.md's R5 row (line 314) says what follows from that answer: "If the display does not isolate its VBUS, R5 states it as a conflict". P2 did this in its report "display VBUS conflict". The direct connection puts a requirement on the switch in one direction only: the display back-feeding the IO board. The list names that requirement twice. "Reverse current blocked" comes from V266, which the owner answered "Yes" unconditionally, so it is stronger than anything conditioned on V80. "5 V back-fed with the input at 0 V" is up to 5.5 V on OUT, survived and blocked, from V81 and V266. The other direction, link power reaching the host's VBUS through Type_C2, is a property of the display that the switch cannot prevent. No answer and no IOBoard.md line sets a switch requirement for it. IOBoard.md:423 states it as "not specified as safe". The rule asks for requirements to be named, not for every value-found row to be cited. A value found for research that sets no part requirement leaves no gap in the list. The verifier itself states "No value in the list is weaker". V79's 4.5 V is carried as the switch's 90 mV share of the display-end budget: 4.825 V − 4.5 V = 325 mV, of which the switch takes 45 mOhm max × 2 A = 90 mV and the cable the remaining 235 mV. That is a derivation from V79, not a weakening of it. IOBoard.md:64 and 368–370 set 5 V, 2 A peak and 1.5 A continuous from the selected source, and the list names all three.

figures.evidence: Facts hold (SLUSEN5A 5.1: SRP with respect to SRN -0.3 to 0.3 V abs max; 5.3: RBAT_SNS 5 mOhm), but the inference that the 60 A pack current crosses RBAT_SNS does not: the Simplified Schematic and Figure 7-1 (page 59) put RBAT_SNS between the converter output and the node joined to both BATTERY and SYSTEM (CSYS), and 6.3.5 says 'connect the system load directly in parallel to the battery pack'. Pack discharge to the load bypasses RBAT_SNS, so 0.300 V at 60 A and 0.334 V at 66.8 A do not occur; only converter output current (charge plus load share from the 15 W input) crosses it. data.ruling: The datasheet verifier's refutation holds on both figures. The stock verifier raised no refutation. 1) Discharge floor: the pack's maker forbids the board's floor. The maker is StefansLipoShop GmbH, named as Hersteller in the product page's GPSR (General Product Safety Regulation) block. Its safety notes (REV.1.06, 14.08.2024), linked from this product page as the "Sicherheitshinweise für SLS LiPo Akkus", set 3.3 V a cell under load and 3.75 V at rest. Its guide sets 3.3 V under load "auch nicht kurzzeitig" and 3.70 V at rest. No source permits 3.0 V a cell. The board disconnects only at 3.0 V a cell (F9, IOBoard.md Discharge floor; owner 2026-09-30), so the board discharges each cell 0.3 V below the maker's limit under load. 2) Temperature: the owner set the pack's limits to 0 to 55 °C, and the board's ambient is 0 to 50 °C (V7). The maker's guide makes preheating mandatory below 18 °C for loads above 5C ("wenn die Akkutemperatur unter 18°C ist, ist Vorwärmen Pflicht"). Near 10 °C it puts the recommended rate under 50 % of the C rate: under 15C, 45 A. The board's about 49.7 A nominal is 16.6C on 3.0 Ah. That is above 5C at every pack temperature from 0 to 18 °C, and above 45 A near 10 °C. The bench has no preheating. Scope is function: both failures concern this function's requirement values: the 3.0 V floor, and 0 to 55 °C at about 49.7 A. They do not concern lifecycle, end-of-life notices, the allowlist or LCSC identity. The owner chose this pack (2026-09-30), and no next-ranked candidate exists. Both conflicts therefore go to the owner rather than to a new verifier pair. The owner's 3.0 V decision (F9, IOBoard.md Pack cells) rests on the reading that the vendor states no per-cell floor. The safety notes linked from the same product page do state one.

data.ruling: The refutation stands. The figure drops the BQ25713 because it allows "10 or 20 mOhm RSR only". The datasheet does not say that. SLUSD83C 9.6.3 says other RSR values can be used, with no more than 20 mOhm suggested. The 10 and 20 mOhm limit in 9.3 applies only to the PSYS (system power monitor) function. REG0x31[2] RSNS_RSR is the PSYS and current-scaling selection, not a limit on the resistor. With a 5 mOhm RSR, the BQ25713's SRP-SRN is 0.249 V at 49.7 A and 0.300 V at 60 A (V284's overcurrent threshold). Both are inside the -0.5 to 0.5 V of 8.1 (absolute maximum) and 8.3 (recommended operating). That is the same margin the figure grants the BQ25723 at 5 mOhm. The figure has a second error. At 10 mOhm and 49.7 A, 0.497 V is below the 0.5 V limit, not above it. Only the 60 A case, 0.60 V, exceeds the limit at 10 mOhm. The figure's other numbers are correct: 0.249 V and 0.300 V, and 12.35 W and 18 W in the resistor. Scope is function: the error is in how this function's battery-path requirement is applied, not in the part's status. With 5 mOhm, every current register (ChargeCurrent, which is 64 mA per step at 10 mOhm) and every ADC reading of battery current scales by 2. PSYS is not usable unless RSR is 10 or 20 mOhm. These are design consequences. They do not disqualify the part.
data.evidence: SLUSD83C (revised May 2023), 9.6.3 Charge current: "The SRP and SRN pins are used to sense voltage drop across RSR with default value of 10 mΩ. However, resistors of other values can also be used. For a larger sense resistor, a larger sense voltage is given, and a higher regulation accuracy; but, at the expense of higher conduction loss. A current sensing resistor value no more than 20 mΩ is suggested." 9.3 PSYS: "For proper PSYS functionality, RAC and RSR values are limited to 10 mΩ and 20 mΩ." REG0x31[2] RSNS_RSR: 0b 10 mΩ (default), 1b 20 mΩ. 8.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings and 8.3 Recommended Operating Conditions, differential SRP-SRN: -0.5 V to 0.5 V. Computed: 5 mΩ x 49.7 A = 0.2485 V; 5 mΩ x 60 A = 0.300 V; 10 mΩ x 49.7 A = 0.497 V (< 0.5 V); 10 mΩ x 60 A = 0.600 V (> 0.5 V); (49.7 A)^2 x 5 mΩ = 12.35 W; (60 A)^2 x 5 mΩ = 18.0 W. data.ruling: The refutation stands. The data sheet's facts are as the re-rank states: SRP with respect to SRN is -0.3 to 0.3 V absolute maximum (5.1), and RBAT_SNS is 5 mOhm (5.3). The inference that the pack's 60 A trip current or 66.8 A crosses RBAT_SNS does not follow from the data sheet. The BQ25756 has no BATFET and no driver pin for one. Its Simplified Schematic (page 1) and Figure 7-1 (page 59) place RBAT_SNS between the converter's output capacitor (SRP side) and the node that joins BATTERY and SYSTEM/CSYS (SRN side). Section 6.3.5.1.2.1 recommends connecting the system load directly in parallel to the battery pack, which is the SRN-side node. Current from the pack to the load therefore does not cross RBAT_SNS. Only the converter's output current crosses it. From a 15 W USB-C input (F8), that current is at most about 2.5 A at the 6.0 V floor before losses (computed), about 12.5 mV across 5 mOhm, inside the 0.3 V rating. The 0.300 V at 60 A and 0.334 V at 66.8 A do not occur, so the stated reason for the drop fails. Other grounds may still exclude the part, but this ruling does not decide them. One example: IOBoard.md line 408 requires termination on the pack's current, not the load's, and this topology measures the converter's output current, the sum of charge and load current. Scope is function: the ruling concerns this function's current requirement, not the part's lifecycle or identity.

Figure 7-1 (page 59, rendered and inspected), from left to right: Q4 drain, then the 80 uF output capacitor, then the SRP tap, then RBAT_SNS 5 mOhm, then the SRN tap. SYSTEM with CSYS and the 4S battery's positive terminal join at the SRN node. The page 1 Simplified Schematic has the same arrangement. The pin table has no BATFET driver pin. data.ruling: The refutation stands. The re-rank's stated reason is false: the 60 A trip and the 66.8 A pack current do not cross RBAT_SNS. The reason assumes the pack's discharge to the bench flows through SRP-SRN. In the data sheet's topology, RBAT_SNS (5 mOhm) sits between the converter's output and one node that joins BATTERY and SYSTEM. Pack-to-load current therefore bypasses the sense resistor. The SRP-SRN absolute maximum of -0.3 to 0.3 V (5.1) is not loaded by the pack current. That makes the arithmetic of 0.300 V at 60 A and 0.334 V at 66.8 A irrelevant. The data sheet's own note in 6.3.5.1.2.1 recommends this topology: "connect the system load directly in parallel to the battery pack". The re-rank cites that same note, which contradicts its own premise. The drop as stated does not hold. This ruling is only about the reason given. It does not qualify the part for the Power path. The topology also implies a separate point, which no verifier raised here and which needs its own reading: RBAT_SNS carries the charge current plus any system load, so the charger does not terminate on the pack's current alone (IOBoard.md line 408). The data sheet also describes no BATFET or power-path stage, which was P2's observation. Scope is function: the finding is about how this function's pack-current requirement applies to the part, not about lifecycle, maker or LCSC identity.
data.evidence: SLUSEN5A (REVISED AUGUST 2026), read again for this ruling, gives the following. Simplified Schematic (page 1): the converter output (Q4 side, CSYS cap) feeds RBAT_SNS. The lower end of RBAT_SNS (SRN) is one node with SYSTEM (+CSYS) and BATTERY, and FB is tapped from it. Figure 7-1 (page 59): "RBAT_SNS 5mΩ" runs between the converter's 80 µF output node (SRP side, through 10 Ω) and the node labelled SYSTEM (80 µF, CSYS). The BATTERY (4S Li-Ion) connects to that same lower node. 6.3.5.1.2.1: "Note that when the system is directly connected to the input supply, the device cannot limit the system load. ... it is recommended to connect the system load directly in parallel to the battery pack." 5.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings: "ACP with respect to ACN, SRP with respect to SRN -0.3 to 0.3 V". 5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions: RBAT_SNS NOM 5 mΩ. VICHG_OC (VSRP - VSRN rising) 120 to 170 mV, a charge-direction limit. With the load parallel to the pack, the pack's discharge into the bench does not pass through RBAT_SNS. Nothing in the data sheet places the 60 A or 66.8 A pack current across SRP-SRN.
